label: GPT-6.1 Sol
output:
## Lee — worth buying a dumper between us?

I reckon it’s worth going halves on this secondhand dumper rather than paying to hire one every time we’ve got a bigger job. We’ve worked together long enough to know what we’d use it for, so here’s the sums written down.

**What we’re spending now**

We’ve had the tracked dumper from Sittingbourne for 14 days this year at £85 a day. That’s £1,190 in hire alone, plus £30 delivery each time — roughly £1,600 all in.

The bloke in Faversham wants £1,650 ono for his 2019 500kg tracked dumper. At the asking price, that’s **£825 each**, and we might get a bit off. He says it had new tracks last spring, although we’d want to check those and see it working before handing anything over.

At this year’s use, the purchase price is about a year’s hire money. Even at half that use, it’s roughly two years. That’s before servicing and repairs, obviously — I’m not pretending an older machine won’t need money spending on it.

**It’s not just the hire bill**

We’ve already got three patio digs and the Boughton drive booked for spring. Having our own means it’s there when we need it, without waiting on availability or deliveries.

Remember Hernhill in September? No dumper available, six ton of muck shifted by barrow, two extra days and your back gone for a week. Then there was the delivery that turned up at 11 and cost us half the morning.

**How we’d split it**

- £825 each to buy, unless we negotiate less.
- Keep it under cover in my lean-to at the yard.
- Servicing and normal wear-and-tear repairs split 50/50.
- Fuel charged to whichever job it’s being used on.
- Whoever breaks it through misuse pays for the damage.

If it doesn’t work out, we can sell it and split the money. These things tend to hold their value, though there’s no guarantee we’d get everything back.

Come and have a look with me this Saturday, before someone else has it. No commitment until we’ve both checked it over.
